automation: Unmanned automated people mover on dedicated guideway
narrative: Two unmanned ParkShuttle vehicles collided head-on near a bridge after a communications problem and a supervisory release error allowed both vehicles into the same single-lane section. Connexxion's investigation said the obstacle-detection system reacted but the stopping distance was insufficient for two vehicles approaching one another. No passengers were aboard.

automation: Driverless shuttle pilot with trained attendant onboard
crash_with: Open rear door of parked delivery van
narrative: A PostBus autonomous shuttle carrying three passengers struck the open rear door of a parked delivery van in Sion. Both vehicles sustained light damage and nobody was injured. PostBus temporarily suspended the trial while the project team and manufacturer analyzed the cause, then later resumed and expanded the service.

date_precision: within first operating year ending Oct 2018
automation: Automated shuttle with onboard safety operator
crash_with: Passenger car pulling out / parking maneuver
narrative: Research evaluating the Bad Birnbach automated-shuttle deployment records one real-world crash during the first operating year: a car pulling out struck the front of the shuttle. The authors state the shuttle was not at fault and note that the collision was difficult to avoid once the other vehicle entered its path. Contemporary summaries describe only sheet-metal/property damage.
verification: Confirmed event; exact day not public in sources reviewed

automation: Automated shuttle pilot with onboard attendant
narrative: A Navya shuttle in Vienna's Seestadt pilot was involved in a low-speed collision with a pedestrian. Wiener Linien said witnesses reported that the pedestrian, wearing headphones and looking at a phone, moved into the side of the bus. She sustained minor scratches. Operations were suspended while vehicle data were reviewed and later resumed.

automation: Automated shuttle in mixed traffic; onboard/remote supervision
narrative: During the 2020 Ülemiste City autonomous-shuttle pilot, an Auve Tech bus collided with a passenger car. A later academic review of Baltic autonomous-bus pilots records the collision and states that the passenger-car driver was at fault. Auve Tech personnel separately described an early Tallinn collision in which a human driver failed to give way and accepted responsibility.
verification: Multiple-source match; exact day not public

automation: Manual takeover by safety operator during automated-shuttle service
narrative: An Auve Tech shuttle in Helsinki's Vuosaari district scratched a parked car while passing a garbage truck. Auve Tech said the safety operator had taken manual control and described the collision as human error. Nobody was injured. The record is retained because it occurred during an automated-shuttle deployment, but the vehicle was under manual control at impact.

automation: Automated shuttle; turning maneuver initiated by onboard operator
narrative: A BVG automated minibus collided with a car while turning at its Tegel terminus. Berlin police said nobody was injured and treated the event as property damage. Police attributed responsibility to the onboard operator, who initiated the turning maneuver while another vehicle was passing; BVG said it would review vehicle data.

The public project material reviewed does not specify the exact crash date, counterpart, injury outcome, or automation state at impact, so those fields remain unknown.

automation: Automated bus service with safety driver onboard
narrative: On the first day carrying passengers, an autonomous e-ATAK bus braked and was struck from behind by a tram in Gothenburg. Västtrafik reported no injuries. Karsan said preliminary technical evaluation indicated that the automated-driving system functioned as designed and that the tram approached from behind.

vehicle: Mustang Mach-E with Wayve AI Driver
automation: Supervised autonomous service; public reporting does not establish whether the Wayve AI Driver or the onboard safety driver was controlling the vehicle at impact
narrative: A Wayve-equipped Ford Mustang Mach-E operating as part of Uber and Wayve's newly launched supervised autonomous ride service was reported in a collision with a Tesla Model Y near Tower Bridge on the day the service launched. Public reporting does not establish fault and does not confirm whether the Wayve AI Driver was engaged or whether the onboard safety driver had taken control at the moment of impact.
verification: Single crash report corroborated by service/vehicle documentation; automation state unconfirmed
